- Overestimate prices after recent spikes; model tends to overshoot post-peak sentiment (e.g., sentiment > 0.6 → forecast too high).
- Underestimate early in the 30-day horizon when sentiment is low (e.g., sentiment < 0.3 → forecast too conservative).
- Mean-reversion bias: model often fails to correct downward after strong upward moves; sentiment > 0.6 → forecast should be capped at 10% below peak.
- Lagged response: model reacts slowly to sentiment shifts; if sentiment drops sharply, forecast should adjust downward by 5–10% within 3–5 days.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts overestimate volatility in high-sentiment periods; reduce forecast spread by 15–20% when sentiment > 0.65.
- Avoid “sentiment echo”: model mirrors sentiment without adjusting for historical mean; subtract 0.1–0.2 from forecast if sentiment > 0.7 and price > 80.
